purpose: Research whether recursive triadic closure, residue-conditioned coupling, and detectable mismatch above a non-zero floor can generate stable relational organization.
core_thesis: space_app, matter_app, and energy_app are co-conditioned projections of the same recursive mismatch process. matter_app and energy_app form an inseparable stabilization/continuation pair within the same process basin.
scope_guardrail: Analogy/projection layer only. This tool does not claim to simulate physical spacetime, real quarks, or fundamental physics directly.

conceptual_model.node: Minimal distinguishability carrier; crudely quark_app-like only at the analogy layer.
conceptual_model.triad: Smallest recursively stable mismatch structure detectable above the floor.
conceptual_model.triad_system: A coupled set of triads exchanging residue-conditioned mismatch through coupling channels.
conceptual_model.residue: History left by prior continuation; alters future admissibility, orientation, and coupling.
conceptual_model.space_app: Ordered relational extension between stabilized recursive mismatch basins.
conceptual_model.floor: Minimum non-zero detectable mismatch threshold below which persistence cannot be stably reinforced.

recursive_reinforcement_channel.role: Writes residue/history and reinforces local closure.

coupling_channel.role: Bidirectional cross-triad exchange conditioned by residue.

triad_definition.relation: Triad exists when three nodes form a recursively stable detectable mismatch closure.

operators.<->_x: Projection/coupling operator binding space_app, matter_app, and energy_app into one inseparable process state unless procedurally decoupled.

small_run_mode.purpose: Correctness, debugging, scalar comparison, hot-path validation.

large_run_mode.sync_policy: Batched layer boundaries, not per-step ping-pong.

layered_pipeline: AVX2 reinjects corrections into next local pass.

memory_policy.shared_memory: Use unified/shared memory for UHD 770 visibility.
memory_policy.ownership_rule: Avoid CPU and GPU writing the same buffer at the same time.
